source_name: World Bank Open Knowledge Repository / Documents & Reports — Montenegro corpus
why_relevant: Full-text searchable archive of World Bank analytical work on Montenegro (including Montenegrin-language editions, e.g. the 'Crna Gora: Priprema za prosperitet' report), development policy operations with financial-sector prior actions, and FSAP-linked technical assistance. Best single pointer for discovering less-visible assessments.

source_name: EBRD — Transition Report country assessment: Montenegro
why_relevant: The annual Transition Report Montenegro assessment flags concrete regulatory pressure points — e.g. political pressure on the central bank over lending-rate caps, AML/CFT framework gaps, and real-estate inflow risks — often earlier and more bluntly than domestic sources. EBRD country strategies also set financial-sector reform conditionality.

source_name: EIB / Vienna Initiative — CESEE Bank Lending Survey
why_relevant: Semi-annual survey of ~15 international banking groups and ~85 local subsidiaries covering Montenegro; captures parent-bank strategy toward the Montenegrin market, credit supply/demand conditions and NPL trends. Indirect for regulation, but a strong leading indicator of where supervisory attention will land.

source_name: S&P Global Ratings — Montenegro sovereign rating actions and research updates
why_relevant: Sovereign rating rationales contain a structured banking-sector section (BICRA-style commentary, credit growth, external position, EU-parent bank funding). Rating actions are dated, scheduled (published sovereign review calendar) and freely readable in the EU regulatory-disclosure section without subscription.

source_name: Moody's Ratings — Montenegro sovereign credit opinion and global banking outlooks
why_relevant: Moody's affirmed Montenegro at Ba3 and moved the outlook to positive (reported March 2026) explicitly citing EU-accession progress; its credit opinions discuss banking-system health and contingent liabilities. Moody's also owns the Basel-AML-Index-adjacent KYC analytics used in country-risk screening.

source_name: Basel Institute on Governance — Basel AML Index (public ranking edition)
why_relevant: Composite ML/TF country risk score built from ~17 public sources including FATF/MONEYVAL evaluation data; gives a comparable annual Montenegro risk trajectory that correspondent banks and compliance teams actually use. Useful as an aggregator that translates the Montenegrin AML framework into a comparable number.

source_name: US State Department — INCSR Volume II (Money Laundering), Montenegro country chapter
why_relevant: Annual, dated, third-country assessment of Montenegro's AML regime naming specific structural weaknesses (financial-investigation capacity, inter-agency cooperation, judicial independence, laundering via construction/real estate and games of chance). Frequently more candid than EU/CoE texts and used by correspondent banks in de-risking decisions.

source_name: GRECO (Council of Europe) — Montenegro evaluation and compliance reports
why_relevant: GRECO compliance reports set dated recommendation-implementation deadlines on integrity, beneficial ownership and law-enforcement governance that overlap with AML/CFT obligations on financial institutions. Reports are published in both English and Montenegrin on rm.coe.int, making it a rare bilingual assessor source.

source_name: Government of Montenegro (gov.me) — official Montenegrin-language reporting on MONEYVAL/IMF outcomes
why_relevant: The Montenegrin authorities' own local-language read-out of external assessments is the fastest indicator of which assessor recommendations the government intends to act on and by when. It names the specific legal instruments amended (Zakon o sprječavanju pranja novca i finansiranja terorizma, pravilnici) and the plenary dates — a bridge between the assessor cell and domestic implementation.

source_name: Uprava za sprječavanje pranja novca i finansiranja terorizma (Montenegro FIU) — national reporting to assessors
why_relevant: The Montenegrin FIU is the national counterpart that drafts the country's MONEYVAL follow-up submissions and national risk assessments; its documents are the domestic mirror of the assessor cycle and are published in Montenegrin via gov.me/wapi.gov.me download endpoints.

source_name: eucrim (Max Planck / EU criminal-law journal) — MONEYVAL & GRECO Montenegro report digests
why_relevant: Concise, reliably dated English digests of each new MONEYVAL/GRECO Montenegro report with direct links to the primary PDFs. An efficient low-volume tripwire for detecting that a new assessor report exists before building the full crawl.

source_name: Radio Slobodna Evropa (RFE/RL Balkan Service) — local-language coverage of assessor processes
why_relevant: Investigative local-language reporting on the politics of external assessment — e.g. coverage of Montenegro lobbying to avoid enhanced AML monitoring. Captures the pre-decision phase (lobbying, negotiation, contested findings) that official assessor documents never record.

source_name: Uprava policije – Sektor za finansijsko-obavještajne poslove (FIU Montenegro) – official site
why_relevant: Montenegro's Financial Intelligence Unit (formerly Uprava za sprječavanje pranja novca i finansiranja terorizma, now a sector of the Police Administration) is the primary AML/CFT authority for obliged entities including banks, payment institutions and e-money issuers. Its site carries news, the legal framework, sanctions-list updates and the 'ZA OBVEZNIKE' section that drives reporting duties.

source_name: FIU Montenegro – 'Za obveznike' (obliged entities) page
why_relevant: Operational compliance hub: electronic reporting of cash, suspicious and other transactions; table of activity codes for obliged entities under Art. 4(2)(13) of the AML/CFT Law; ML/TF typologies; beneficial-owner identification instructions. This is where reporting obligations and formats for banks/payment firms are set out.

source_name: Komisija za tržište kapitala Crne Gore (Capital Market Authority) – official site
why_relevant: Independent securities/capital-market regulator (IOSCO/ESMA-aligned). Publishes regulations (Regulativa), forms, warnings about unlicensed operators, market-participant registers, and news. Directly relevant to banks with investment services, custody, fund business and to payment firms crossing into investment services.

source_name: Komisija za tržište kapitala – javne rasprave / nacrti pravila (draft rules consultations)
why_relevant: Consultation drafts of subordinate rules are posted as dated PDF folders (e.g. 'Nacrti-pravila-26.02.2026'). This is the earliest visible signal of forthcoming capital-market obligations and their comment deadlines.

source_name: Komisija za tržište kapitala – SPNFT (AML/CFT) section
why_relevant: The capital market authority is itself an AML/CFT supervisor for its licensees; this section carries its own AML guidance and supervisory expectations, separate from the CBCG and FIU streams.

source_name: Agencija za zaštitu ličnih podataka i slobodan pristup informacijama (AZLP) – official site
why_relevant: Montenegro's DPA. Publishes opinions (mišljenja), recommendations (preporuke), supervisory decisions (rješenja), registries of data collections, forms and annual reports. Banks and payment firms face direct obligations here (video surveillance, direct marketing, biometrics, cross-border transfers, breach handling) and inspection findings against named controllers are published.

source_name: AZLP – supervisory decisions archive (rješenja, by year)
why_relevant: Year-foldered archive of individual supervisory decisions naming controllers, including public bodies and companies. High-value for tracking enforcement patterns and what the DPA actually penalises — a leading indicator of compliance risk for financial-sector controllers.

source_name: ANO – AML/CFT obligations page for insurance obliged entities
why_relevant: Sets out how the AML/CFT Law applies to insurance-sector obliged entities under ANO supervision — a compliance stream distinct from CBCG and FIU guidance and easily missed if 'the regulator' is treated as one body.

source_name: Uprava za inspekcijske poslove – Tržišna inspekcija (Market Inspection)
why_relevant: The inspection authority whose Market Inspection department enforces the Consumer Protection Law, including consumers' economic interests, advertising of products and services, and consumer complaints. It publishes annual work reports and work programmes that reveal inspection priorities and complaint volumes touching financial services.

source_name: Ministarstvo finansija – Javne rasprave (public consultations)
why_relevant: The Ministry of Finance is the sponsor of most financial-sector legislation (AML/CFT law, financial conglomerates, tax mechanisms). Its consultations page carries drafts and deadlines before they reach the regulators' implementing acts. Note: the ministry appears under both mif.gov.me and gov.me article URLs — track both.

source_name: Agencija za sprječavanje korupcije (ASK) – anti-corruption agency and public registers
why_relevant: Integrity body maintaining public registers of officials' income/asset declarations, conflicts of interest, lobbyists and gift records. These registers are the practical domestic source for PEP identification and enhanced due diligence by Montenegrin banks, and ASK also issues integrity-plan and whistleblowing guidance.

source_name: MONEYVAL (Council of Europe) – Montenegro country page and follow-up reports
why_relevant: Montenegro's 5th-round MER was adopted December 2023 and it remains in enhanced follow-up, with follow-up reports adopted at the 70th Plenary (Dec 2025) and a further report due within a year. These reports are the single best forward-looking indicator of what Montenegrin AML supervisors will demand of banks and payment firms next.

source_name: CEZAP – Centar za zaštitu potrošača Crne Gore (consumer protection NGO)
why_relevant: The main Montenegrin consumer NGO (est. 1999), an active participant in drafting the Consumer Protection Law under which banking, credit, insurance, investment and payment-transaction services are classified as financial services. Its news and campaigns reveal consumer complaint themes and pending regulatory pressure on banks before authorities act.

source_name: Javna rasprava reports on the Draft Consumer Protection Law (wapi.gov.me document endpoint)
why_relevant: Post-consultation reports list every comment received and the ministry's acceptance/rejection — a direct read on how consumer-protection obligations over financial services were shaped. Demonstrates that gov.me serves its PDFs from the wapi.gov.me endpoint, which is the pattern to target when harvesting Montenegrin government documents generally.

source_name: Uprava prihoda i carina Crne Gore (Revenue and Customs Administration) – FATCA/AEOI reporting
why_relevant: Non-CBCG authority imposing reporting duties directly on Montenegrin financial institutions: the FATCA agreement with the US has been in force since 2018 and AEOI/CRS implementation has been repeatedly delayed. Any CRS go-live decision creates hard reporting deadlines for banks. Coverage is thin and needs manual confirmation.
